correctness.rationale: The distance-two adjacency is exactly the total graph. All its cliques are classified into old-vertex cliques, vertex-star simplices, edge triangles, and exceptional midpoint triangles. Every nonexceptional star face is removed by a finite explicit elementary-collapse matching uniquely determined by its common vertex, then each edge-midpoint is removed by two free-face collapses. Each exceptional midpoint-triangle boundary is homotopic, via explicitly named triangles, to the original filled graph triangle, hence null. A standard CW attachment lemma proves the homotopy wedge. The triple long exact sequence identifies canonical integral relative homology and orientation-signed symmetry. The supplied standard-library program exhaustively cross-checks all 772 connected labeled graphs on up to five vertices.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial metric scale of edge subdivisions is a natural operation on any finite graph; it is not a contrived finite slice. The universal formula isolates one independently meaningful two-sphere for every triangle while preserving every original higher homotopy feature, and the canonical oriented triangle module determines equivariant integral relative homology for arbitrary automorphism groups. In particular it extends a published complete-graph special case and the known pi_1 result and distinguishes triangle-rich from triangle-free graphs at scale two, with meaningful use in graph subdivisions and graph-valued topology.
